prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one 4:3 landscape painting for The Burnt Book Sanskrit learning story. Request 1536 x 1152 native output or the closest supported native 4:3 resolution. Refined Indian watercolor with restrained gouache on warm ivory paper; organic detail, quiet ochre, sage, dusty terracotta, muted indigo. Warm, gentle, evocative storytelling, consistent character design.
Canonical scene brief: A village house at night: two dusty travelling scholars with cloth bundles sitting in the courtyard with a lamp; in the lane beyond, a travelling actor dancing to a drum, torch-lit; a small boy of seven watching from the doorway, head tilted, listening; his mother in the doorway beside him.
Character appearances:
vararuci: A small, bright-eyed boy of about seven in a plain white dhoti, a thin sacred thread, hair in a short tuft, always listening with his head tilted.
vasudatta: A slim young widow in a plain white-grey sari, tired kind eyes, a clay lamp always near her hand.
vyadi: A lean scholar in a travel-worn ochre dhoti, dusty feet, a cloth bundle of palm leaves on one shoulder, tired but eager eyes.
indradatta: A broad, quiet scholar in a faded saffron wrap, a staff, a thoughtful frown, walking beside Vyāḍi.
Phone-first composition: clear compact narrative grouping, essential faces, hands and objects comfortably inside all edges. Show the complete scene without border. No collage or multi-panel layout.
Writing is permitted by the owner. This particular scene needs no readable inscription; focus on its narrative. Do not invent scripts or fill small objects with pseudo-lettering. No watermark or UI.

sources.title: Kathāsaritsāgara, taraṅga 2 (Digital Corpus of Sanskrit file KSS, 1, 2), the story retold in new, simple sentences with two real verses quoted
sources.note: The plot follows Somadeva's text: two scholars seek a pupil who holds what he hears once; they find a boy; a voice from the sky foretells his future; they take him to the teacher Varṣa. The two quoted verses are Somadeva's own words; the rest is new Sanskrit in the present tense.

image.brief: A village house at night: two dusty travelling scholars with cloth bundles sitting in the courtyard with a lamp; in the lane beyond, a travelling actor dancing to a drum, torch-lit; a small boy of seven watching from the doorway, head tilted, listening; his mother in the doorway beside him.

alt.en: Two travelling scholars in a courtyard at night as a small boy listens to a drum in the lane
alt.hi: रात में आँगन में दो यात्री विद्वान्, गली में मृदंग सुनता नन्हा बालक

meaning.en: Two scholars come to the house.
They stay in the house at night.
meaning.hi: वे रात में घर में ठहरते हैं।

meaning.en: There is the sound of a drum.

meaning.hi: वह सब कुछ याद रखता है।

image.brief: The mother standing at the door of the small house at night with her hand on her small son's shoulder, looking up at the night sky where faint golden lines of script and a soft glow gather above the roof; the two scholars at her feet looking up in wonder; the boy listening with his head tilted.

alt.en: A mother and her small son look up at a golden glow in the night sky, two scholars beside them
alt.hi: माता और नन्हा बालक रात के आकाश में सुनहरी आभा देखते, पास में दो विद्वान्

meaning.en: The boy says the lesson again.
meaning.hi: बालक वह पाठ फिर बोलता है।
विद्वान् विस्मय में पड़ जाते हैं।

meaning.en: The scholars say: “We two seek one who holds what he hears.”
meaning.hi: विद्वान् कहते हैं: “हम दोनों सुना हुआ धारण करने वाले को खोज रहे हैं।”

gloss.en: one who holds what he hears

passage.sa: एष श्रुतधरो जातो विद्यां वर्षादवाप्स्यति किंच व्याकरणं लोके प्रतिष्ठां प्रापयिष्यति

meaning.en: “This one holds what he hears, he will get knowledge from Varṣa, and he will give grammar its place in the world.” (Somadeva, Kathāsaritsāgara, taraṅga 2)
meaning.hi: “यह सुना हुआ धारण करता है; वह वर्ष से विद्या पाएगा, और व्याकरण को संसार में प्रतिष्ठा दिलाएगा।” (सोमदेव, कथासरित्सागर, तरंग 2)

meaning.en: The mother gives the boy to the two scholars.
meaning.hi: माता बालक को दोनों विद्वानों को सौंप देती है।

title.hi: एक बार, दो बार, तीन बार

image.brief: The courtyard of a poor mud-walled house in Pāṭaliputra: the thin teacher Varṣa seated on swept ground speaking, three boys sitting cross-legged before him with a small boy in front, eyes closed, listening; townsfolk gathering at the gate with folded hands; a royal messenger with a gift tray arriving.

alt.en: A teacher speaks to three pupils in a poor courtyard as townsfolk gather with folded hands
alt.hi: गरीब आँगन में तीन शिष्यों को पढ़ाते गुरु, हाथ जोड़े जुटते नगरवासी

meaning.hi: वे वर्ष के घर पहुँचते हैं।
वर्ष ओंकार का उच्चारण करते हैं।

passage.sa: सकृच्छ्रुतं मया तत्र द्विःश्रुतं व्याडिना तथा त्रिश्रुतं चेन्द्रदत्तेन गुरुणोक्तमगृह्यत

meaning.en: “What the teacher said was taken in: by me after one hearing, by Vyāḍi after two, and by Indradatta after three.” (Somadeva, Kathāsaritsāgara, taraṅga 2)
meaning.hi: “गुरु ने जो कहा वह ग्रहण किया गया: मुझसे एक बार सुनने पर, व्याडि से दो बार सुनने पर, और इन्द्रदत्त से तीन बार सुनने पर।” (सोमदेव, कथासरित्सागर, तरंग 2)

meaning.en: King Nanda gives wealth to Varṣa.
meaning.hi: राजा नन्द वर्ष को धन देता है।
लोग वर्ष को प्रणाम करते हैं।
